<assessment>SOURCE 1 shows the street elevation; SOURCE 2–3 show opposite rear corners, SOURCE 4 the roof, and SOURCE 5–6 opposite front corners. Shared landmarks establish the brick enclosure, dark upper enclosure, raised glazed room, two recessed balconies, narrow front window stack and boundary walls. CURRENT retains these primary elements and broadly matches their arrangement, rear opening count and side opening patterns. No source-backed primary volume is missing. The photograph reveals remaining differences in front window assembly and brick character that the supplied SketchUp references simplify. Screenshots cannot establish concealed connections or confirm watertight joints; no obvious floating primary volume is visible. No dimensions are supplied.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: The lower two sections of the narrow front window stack lack the central vertical mullion visible in SOURCE 1. Its surrounding dark reveal also reads substantially thinner and flatter than the photographed recessed frame.
action: Locally add the lower central mullion and deepen the perimeter reveal/frame to match the photograph, retaining the opening’s position and overall extent.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="front">problem: CURRENT brickwork reads as flat, uniform, regular masonry. SOURCE 1 shows markedly thinner, elongated bricks with irregular faces and pronounced horizontal mortar relief across the main facade and boundary walls.
action: Adjust the brick material scale, surface variation and shallow relief on these visible zones; preserve their existing outlines and openings.</issue>
<keep>Two stacked balconies, with the lower balcony wider than the upper.
Rear arrangement of five individual windows above a central double glazed door.
Three narrow left-side openings and three short right-side openings.
Left front dark cladding’s vertical divisions and intermediate horizontal joint.</keep>
